name: Design History, Culture and Studies
description: This course introduces students to key frameworks, narratives, and debates in design history, culture, and studies. Beginning with historiographical methods, it examines modernism, postmodernism, and global design movements through critical lenses. The course then explores Indian design histories, from colonial exhibitions to post-independence institutions, followed by deeper engagement with craft, culture, and their intersections. It culminates in examining contemporary design cultures, sustainability discourses, and critical design studies. Through seminars, readings, museum visits, and a final essay, students will build a nuanced understanding of design’s social, cultural, and political dimensions, and develop tools for critical reflection and scholarly inquiry.
